source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 7.

sections.heading: 1. Temperature
points: **Temperature** = a measure of the **degree of hotness or coldness** of a body.
Our **sense of touch is unreliable** for measuring temperature (the same water can feel hot or cold depending on the hand) — so we use a **thermometer**.

sections.heading: 2. Thermometers

sub: Has a **kink/constriction** so the reading does not fall until shaken.

points.text: **Laboratory thermometer** — measures a wider range (about **-10°C to 110°C**):

points: **Digital thermometers** are now preferred; **mercury** thermometers are being phased out because mercury is **toxic**.

sections.heading: 3. Reading a Thermometer Correctly
points: Wash a clinical thermometer before and after use; give it a **jerk** to bring the level down.
Read with the **eye level with the top of the liquid/number** (avoid parallax error).
Do not hold the bulb; do not use a clinical thermometer to measure very hot things.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness; measured with a thermometer.
Units: Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F), Kelvin (K = SI unit).
Clinical thermometer range ≈ 35–42°C, has a kink; lab thermometer wider range, no kink.
Mercury is toxic → digital thermometers preferred.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **clinical thermometer** has a **kink** (so the reading holds); the **laboratory thermometer** does not.
Normal body temperature is about **37°C (98.6°F)** — not 98.6°C.
The **SI unit** of temperature is the **Kelvin**, though Celsius is used in daily life.
Our skin/touch cannot reliably measure temperature — a thermometer is needed.
